items.followUp: A pump lifts 50 kg of water through a height of 12 m in 8 s. Calculate its power in watts and horsepower. (Take g = 10 m/s² and 1 hp = 746 W.)

rubric.why: Identifies the given mass, height and time.
rubric.description: Correctly states the given quantities in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when the mass, height and time are correctly identified.

rubric.why: Uses the relation between power and work, and the expression for lifting work.
rubric.description: Writes the appropriate formula for power and gravitational work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for P = W/t together with W = mgh, or an equivalent combined formula.

rubric.why: Shows the calculation and obtains the pump’s power.
rubric.description: Substitutes the values and calculates the power in watts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution and 1 mark for 1120 W.

rubric.why: Converts the power from watts to horsepower.
rubric.description: Uses 1 hp = 746 W and gives the power in horsepower.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversion and answer.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 70 kg, h = 16 m, t = 10 s, g = 10 m/s².
Work done, W = mgh.
Since 1 hp = 746 W, power in horsepower = 1,120 W/746 W = 1.5 hp (approximately).

items.followUp: Describe how a hydraulic lift uses Pascal’s principle to raise a car.

rubric.why: States the principle underlying the hydraulic press.
rubric.description: Explains that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally throughout it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct statement of Pascal’s principle.

rubric.why: Identifies the essential arrangement of a hydraulic press.
rubric.description: Describes two pistons of different areas connected by an enclosed liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the connected liquid and two pistons of different areas.

rubric.why: Shows how pressure relates the forces on the two pistons.
rubric.description: Applies equal pressure at the two pistons using force divided by area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct pressure relation.

rubric.description: States that a small force on the smaller piston produces a larger force on the larger piston, lifting a heavy load.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining force multiplication or the lifting of a heavy load.

modelAnswer: A hydraulic press works on Pascal’s principle: pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally in all directions.
It consists of two pistons of different cross-sectional areas connected by a pipe containing an enclosed liquid.
A force F₁ on the smaller piston of area A₁ produces pressure P = F₁/A₁ in the liquid.
The same pressure acts on the larger piston, so F₂/A₂ = F₁/A₁.
Because A₂ is larger than A₁, the force F₂ is larger; it can lift or press a heavy load.

items.followUp: What is a measuring cylinder? How can it be used to find the volume of an irregular solid?

rubric.why: Defines the instrument by its form and purpose.
rubric.description: Identifies a measuring cylinder as a graduated vessel used to measure liquid volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: States a valid use of the instrument.
rubric.description: Gives measuring liquid volumes or finding an irregular solid’s volume by displacement as a use.

modelAnswer: A measuring cylinder is a graduated cylindrical vessel used to measure the volume of liquids.
It is used to measure liquid volumes and to find the volume of an irregular solid by the displacement method.

rubric.why: Provides the textbook definition of atomic physics.
rubric.description: Defines atomic physics as the branch of physics concerned with the structure and properties of atoms.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a complete definition; award 1 mark for identifying it as a branch of physics dealing with atoms.

modelAnswer: Atomic physics is the branch of physics that deals with the structure and properties of atoms.

items.followUp: A race lasts 18 seconds. Explain how you would use a stopwatch to measure its duration.

rubric.why: Starts timing at the correct event.
rubric.description: Starts the stopwatch when the event begins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing when to start it.

rubric.why: Stops and reads the measurement correctly.
rubric.description: Stops the stopwatch when the event ends and reads the elapsed time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stopping at the end and reading the time.

modelAnswer: Press the start button as the event begins.
Press the stop button as the event ends, then read the elapsed time shown on the stopwatch.

items.followUp: Define random motion and give one example from everyday life or science.

rubric.why: Describes the defining feature of random motion.
rubric.description: States that random motion has no fixed, regular path or direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of random motion.
rubric.description: Gives an appropriate example, such as the motion of gas molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid example.

modelAnswer: Random motion is motion in which an object moves irregularly without a fixed path or direction.
The random motion of gas molecules is an example.

items.followUp: Classify each quantity as a scalar or vector: mass, temperature, force and velocity.

rubric.description: States that a scalar has magnitude only and no direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition of a scalar.

rubric.description: States that a vector has both magnitude and direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition of a vector.

modelAnswer: A scalar quantity has magnitude only and no direction.
A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction.

items.followUp: What is inertia? Give one example showing its effect.

rubric.why: Defines inertia in terms of resistance to a change in motion.
rubric.description: States that inertia is the tendency of a body to resist a change in its state of rest or uniform motion.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the complete definition; award 1 mark for identifying resistance to a change in motion.

modelAnswer: Inertia is the tendency of a body to resist a change in its state of rest or uniform motion.
